data.title: Rapamycin co-exposure fails to reduce cisplatin-induced damage in GC6-spg spermatogonial cell line.
data.authors: Jibrin A, Mitchell RT, Lopes F

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Rapamycin did not protect a mouse spermatogonial cell line from cisplatin damage in vitro, unlike reports in female fertility models.
data.abstract_excerpt: This study assessed whether rapamycin could protect male spermatogonial stem cells (GC6-spg line) from cisplatin-induced cytotoxicity, analogous to its protective role reported in female fertility preservation. Rapamycin co-exposure did not prevent cisplatin-induced cell loss or damage in this spermatogonial cell line, suggesting limited utility for male fertility preservation during cancer treatment.

extracted_findings.target: mTOR inhibition; spermatogonial stem cell survival
extracted_findings.effect: No protective effect – rapamycin does not rescue cisplatin-induced spermatogonial stem cell loss (negative result)
